# paigasus-gateway config. Copy to gateway.toml or supply via GATEWAY_* env vars.
# Precedence: built-in defaults < gateway.toml < GATEWAY_* environment.
#
# LIMITS NOTE (SMA-677): with no [limits] table (the default) there is no rate limit and no spend
# limit on the OpenAI upstream. The [limits] table below adds a per-principal request rate, a
# per-org request rate and a per-org token budget. Keep a hard OpenAI spend cap even then.
# The budget counts tokens, not money. Requests in flight when the budget runs out still
# complete, and the gateway charges them. With backend = "redis", Redis can be unavailable.
# Then the gateway is fail-open: it admits requests with no limit.

# http_addr = "0.0.0.0:8088"          # axum HTTP (chat + health) — default shown
# log_level = "info"                  # RUST_LOG-style filter — default shown

# --- Egress timeouts/limits (D6) ---

# connect_timeout_secs     = 10       # TCP+TLS connect to the OpenAI upstream — default shown
# first_byte_timeout_secs  = 30       # time to the first response byte — default shown
# stream_idle_timeout_secs = 300      # max gap between streamed chunks — default shown
# max_request_bytes        = 1048576  # reject larger request bodies before parsing (1 MiB) —
#                                      # default shown

# Serve streamed (SSE) chat completions (default true). When false, a request carrying
# `stream: true` is rejected with 400 and `param: "stream"`, and the gateway.chat.stream
# capability is not advertised. Non-streaming completions are unaffected.
# stream_enabled = true

# --- IAM gRPC client (G4 dials this for auth/introspection) ---

# [iam]
# grpc_addr = "https://127.0.0.1:9090"   # default shown
# SMA-775: the file that holds the gateway service credential, an IAM API key with the
# tool_policy_reader role. Required when tool_policy.source is kind = "iam". The gateway sends it
# on the two policy fetch calls only, and reads the file again on every fetch, so a rotation needs
# no restart. A trailing newline in the file is ignored. The value is never logged.
# service_credential_file = "/run/secrets/paigasus-gateway-iam-key"

# [iam.tls]
# TLS is the DEFAULT and REQUIRED transport to paigasus-iam: the introspect call carries raw
# caller-presented API keys AND user OIDC bearers, so this link must be encrypted unless you
# explicitly opt out below AND grpc_addr is a loopback host (D8). Default shown (system trust
# store, no mTLS):
# mode                = "tls"           # "tls" (default) | "loopback_insecure"
# # ca_cert_path      = "/path/to/ca.pem"       # unset = system trust store only
# # client_cert_path  = "/path/to/client.pem"   # mTLS — set together with client_key_path
# # client_key_path   = "/path/to/client-key.pem"
#
# ONLY valid when grpc_addr resolves to a loopback host (127.0.0.0/8, localhost, ::1) — e.g.
# a local dev IAM instance on the same machine with no TLS cert provisioned:
# [iam.tls]
# mode = "loopback_insecure"

# --- OpenAI upstream (G6 forwards chat-completions requests here) ---

# [upstream.openai]
# base_url = "https://api.openai.com"    # default shown
#
# REQUIRED — no valid default (the empty-string default fails `GatewayConfig::validate`, not
# figment extraction — an unset key loads fine but boot refuses to start). NEVER put this in
# gateway.toml; source it from the environment so it never lands in a config file or VCS:
# GATEWAY_UPSTREAM__OPENAI__API_KEY=sk-...
#
# Extra trust anchors for the upstream calls — a path to a PEM bundle, for a self-hosted
# vLLM/LiteLLM endpoint behind a corporate CA. ADDS to the trust store; the OPPOSITE of
# [iam.tls] ca_cert_path, which PINS. ROOTS ONLY: every certificate here becomes an unconstrained
# trust anchor for every request the upstream egress client makes, to any host it reaches — not
# for the whole process. Read once at boot. A bare self-signed leaf
# also works when this bundle holds that leaf's own PEM, though a private CA is tidier once
# more than one host is involved.
# extra_ca_bundle_path = "/etc/paigasus/corp-ca.pem"

# --- Metrics (SMA-446 Unit 2: Prometheus `GET /metrics`) ---

# [metrics]
# enabled = true                # default shown; false skips installing the recorder entirely —
#                                # no /metrics route, no metrics-facade recorder in this process
# addr = "127.0.0.1:9091"       # optional separate internal listener; RECOMMENDED for a public
#                                # gateway so /metrics never shares a port with public traffic.
#                                # unset (default) merges /metrics onto http_addr instead. MUST
#                                # differ from http_addr (rejected by GatewayConfig::validate).

# --- DPoP (SMA-700): proof-of-possession tokens on the protected routes ---
#
# Off by default. With enabled = true, a client may send `Authorization: DPoP <token>` with one
# `DPoP` proof header (RFC 9449). The gateway forwards the proof, the method and the path to IAM,
# which checks it against its authn.dpop.forwarded_base_urls. Turn DPoP on in IAM first.
# A 401 then carries `WWW-Authenticate: DPoP algs="ES256 RS256"`. The API-key leg does not run for
# the DPoP scheme. A client must make a NEW proof for each attempt: a retry that sends the same
# proof again is refused as a replay.
# [dpop]
# enabled = false                       # default shown; env GATEWAY_DPOP__ENABLED

# --- Limits (SMA-677): request rate and token budget on POST /v1/chat/completions ---
#
# Off unless this table exists. An unset key means no limit on that dimension. The value 0 is
# rejected. A misspelt key fails the boot. A table with no limit value set builds no store and
# opens no Redis connection. The gateway logs one info line. Refusals: 429 "rate-limited"
# (Retry-After, retryable) and 429 "budget-exhausted" (type "insufficient_quota",
# x-should-retry: false).
#
# [limits]
# backend = "memory"                     # "memory" (default) | "redis"
#   # memory: one process only. With N replicas the limits are about N times the values below.
#   # A restart sets every budget to zero. Use "redis" for more than one replica.
# # redis_url: set GATEWAY_LIMITS__REDIS_URL, never this file. The URL can carry a password.
# # Required for backend = "redis". Rejected for "memory". Use rediss:// outside a private network.
# # Redis requirements:
# #   - Redis 6.2 or later.
# #   - A URL that always reaches the primary. Do not use a replica or Redis Cluster.
# #   - A dedicated instance for limits, or at least a dedicated logical database.
# #   - maxmemory-policy noeviction, or enough headroom that eviction never runs.
# #     An evicted budget key silently resets the budget of that org.
# #   - appendonly yes, if budgets must survive a Redis restart.
# # Redis must be reachable at boot. A gateway with backend = "redis" does not start while
# # Redis is down. After boot, fail-open applies: when Redis is unavailable, the gateway
# # admits requests with no limit and charges no tokens until Redis recovers. See
# # RUNBOOK-observability.md, "Gateway limits: fail-open and Redis requirements".
# principal_requests_per_minute = 60     # unset: no principal rate limit; max 1000000000
# org_requests_per_minute       = 600    # unset: no org rate limit (summed over the org's principals); max 1000000000
# tokens_per_period             = 5000000 # unset: no token budget; max 1000000000000
# budget_period                 = "monthly" # "daily" | "weekly" (ISO week) | "monthly" (default), UTC
#
# Per-org overrides, by org UUID. TOML only: environment variables cannot set an array of
# tables. With backend = "redis", give EVERY replica the same list, or two replicas apply
# different limits to one shared count. A field you leave out keeps the table default.
# [[limits.org]]
# id                      = "0190a100-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a1"
# org_requests_per_minute = 1200
# tokens_per_period       = 20000000
#
# [[limits.org]]
# id     = "0190a100-0000-7000-8000-0000000000b2"
# exempt = true                          # no org rate and no budget; the principal rate still applies
#
# Environment: GATEWAY_LIMITS__BACKEND, GATEWAY_LIMITS__REDIS_URL,
# GATEWAY_LIMITS__PRINCIPAL_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE, GATEWAY_LIMITS__ORG_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE,
# GATEWAY_LIMITS__TOKENS_PER_PERIOD, GATEWAY_LIMITS__BUDGET_PERIOD.
#
# Charging: a stream is charged its reported usage only when the client sends
# stream_options: {"include_usage": true} (the console playground does). Otherwise the gateway
# charges an estimate: about one token per streamed record plus the prompt text / 4.

# --- Tool-call interception (SMA-749): hold, check and rewrite model tool calls ---
#
# Off by default. With enabled = true the gateway parses every response of
# POST /v1/chat/completions, holds each tool call until its arguments are complete (text keeps
# streaming), asks the decider, and replaces a blocked call with an assistant notice. This build's
# decider allows every call. Each decision is reported as an SSE comment ": paigasus-decision {...}"
# or, for a non-stream answer, in the paigasus-tool-decisions header. A misspelt key fails the boot.
#
# [tool_interception]
# enabled             = false      # env GATEWAY_TOOL_INTERCEPTION__ENABLED
# max_record_bytes    = 1048576    # one SSE record; larger is a failure
# max_held_bytes      = 4194304    # all held bytes of one stream; also the cap on one non-stream body
# max_hold_secs       = 300        # from a tool call's first fragment to its completion
# decide_timeout_secs = 5
# keepalive_secs      = 10         # ": keep-alive" comment while a call is held; < max_hold_secs
# on_failure          = "block"    # "block" (default) | "allow" (observe: forward and report)
#   # A failure is: a record or body that is not strict JSON or not the provider's shape, a
#   # limit above, a decider error, or a stream that ends inside a tool call. With "block", a
#   # non-stream answer that cannot be checked is a 502 "tool-interception-malformed-response".
#
# SMA-769: the OpenAI Responses API route, POST /v1/responses. Off by default; with
# enabled = false the route answers 404. Setting it back to false is the rollback.
#
# [responses]
# enabled           = false      # env GATEWAY_RESPONSES__ENABLED
# max_request_bytes = 16777216   # env GATEWAY_RESPONSES__MAX_REQUEST_BYTES; over this is a 413
# max_record_bytes  = 16777216   # env GATEWAY_RESPONSES__MAX_RECORD_BYTES; one SSE record
# max_held_bytes    = 33554432   # env GATEWAY_RESPONSES__MAX_HELD_BYTES; all held bytes of one stream
#   # Operator notes (spec 9):
#   # 1. The gateway does not rewrite "store". With store = true (the OpenAI default),
#   #    OpenAI keeps the output, a blocked call included, for its retention period.
#   # 2. Hosted execution: OpenAI runs a hosted "shell_call" or a server "tool_search_call"
#   #    itself, even when the report says "block". The gateway cannot hold it, because the
#   #    item class is fixed before these fields are known. The notice replaces the item for
#   #    the client only. The decision log must not count such a block as a prevented action.
#   # 3. With interception on, the route refuses with 400 "responses-stateful-not-supported"
#   #    a request that asks for state on the server. These are: a non-null
#   #    "previous_response_id", "conversation" or "prompt", and an "item_reference" input
#   #    item. An input item with no string "type" and no string "role" counts as an
#   #    "item_reference". "background": true is refused in both modes.
#   # 4. With interception on, the route refuses a request body that has a duplicate JSON key
#   #    at any depth (400, before admission). A duplicate "background" key is refused in
#   #    both modes.
#   # 5. Observe mode ("on_failure" = "allow"): when one item is truncated, the response
#   #    switches to pass-through. A completed call that the policy blocks, in the same
#   #    response, can then reach the client. A stream and a body behave the same.
#   # 6. Rollback: set "enabled" = false. The route then answers 404.
#
# SMA-752: Cedar tool-call decisions (spec 6.4). Off by default; with enabled = false the
# gateway behaves as before. A misspelt key fails at start. Needs [tool_interception] enabled.
#
# WARNING: mode "enforce" with no tenant policies blocks every tool that is not on the floor.
# Cedar denies by default, and no policy permits the call. Load a permit policy for an org
# before you set its mode to "enforce". Use "log_only" first to see what the policy would block.
# A blocked shell_call_output becomes one notice chunk; the real upstream accepts it (SMA-776).
# A blocked computer_call_output has no field for the notice. An enforced block refuses the
# request with a 400 tool-result-unreplaceable. A floor block of "computer" does this in every
# mode. See rs/crates/libs/paigasus-gateway-core/tests/fixtures/request_rewrite/README.md.
#
# [tool_policy]
# enabled               = false      # env GATEWAY_TOOL_POLICY__ENABLED
# on_policy_unavailable = "closed"   # REQUIRED when enabled: "open" | "closed" (D9, D34)
# default_mode          = "off"      # "off" | "log_only" | "enforce"; the mode of an org with no entry (D8)
# refresh_secs          = 30         # 1..=86400
# max_stale_secs        = 300        # 1..=86400; >= refresh_secs
# idle_evict_secs       = 3600       # 1..=86400
# load_timeout_ms       = 1000       # must be < tool_interception.decide_timeout_secs * 1000 (D31)
# source = { kind = "file", dir = "/etc/paigasus/tool-policies" }   # REQUIRED when enabled
#   # SMA-775: source = { kind = "iam" } fetches the compiled sets and the tenant settings (mode and
#   # fail mode) from paigasus-iam. It needs iam.service_credential_file. [[tool_policy.org]]
#   # entries are refused with it, because IAM holds the mode and the fail mode of each org.
#   # The floor is always enforced when enabled (D33). There is no floor_mode.
#
# [tool_policy.nats]                 # optional: policy invalidation events
# url        = "nats://nats:4222"    # never written to logs or dumps
# creds_file = "/etc/nats/creds"
# ca_file    = "/etc/nats/ca.pem"
#
# [[tool_policy.org]]                # TOML only; one entry per org (D7, D34)
# id                    = "0190a100-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a1"
# mode                  = "enforce"
# on_policy_unavailable = "open"     # optional override of the global value

# --- SMA-755: the tool decision log (§ 5.12) ---
# Records each tool-policy decision in a Redis stream, and a relay publishes it to NATS.
# enabled = true needs [tool_policy] enabled = true, redis_url, digest_key, digest_key_id and [decision_log.nats].
# A Redis outage or a NATS outage at boot does not stop the gateway.
#
# [decision_log]
# enabled        = false                         # env GATEWAY_DECISION_LOG__ENABLED
# redis_url      = "redis://redis:6379"          # required when enabled; never written to logs or dumps
# key_prefix     = "paigasus:gateway"            # default shown; must not be empty or padded
# stream_max_len = 100000                        # default shown; at least 1
# queue_capacity = 4096                          # default shown; at least 1
# digest_key     = "change-me-at-least-32-bytes-long-secret"   # required when enabled; at least 32 bytes; never logged
# digest_key_id  = "2026-11"                     # required when enabled; names the key for a rotation
#
# [decision_log.nats]                            # required when enabled
# url        = "nats://nats:4222"                # never written to logs or dumps
# creds_file = "/etc/paigasus/nats/gateway-decision-publisher.creds"
# ca_file    = "/etc/paigasus/nats/ca.pem"       # optional; REPLACES the system trust store (absent: system roots)
feat(rs): rate limit and token budget for gateway chat completions (SMA-677) (#373)
* feat(contracts): add the rate-limited and budget-exhausted gateway reasons

Two gateway registry reasons for SMA-677, regenerated for Rust, Python
and TypeScript. The SDK gains the quota-exhausted presentation, and both
console copy tables gain its row.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(rs): add the gateway rate-window arithmetic

The D3 sliding-window counter of SMA-677 as pure domain functions, with
the integer form that both limit stores share. src/domain.rs moves to
src/domain/mod.rs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(rs): add the gateway budget periods, policy and limit store port

UTC daily, ISO-weekly and monthly budget periods with a relative charge
TTL, the per-request policy with org overrides and exemptions, the D8
refusal precedence, and the async LimitStore port with its fail-open
error kinds (SMA-677).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(rs): add the memory limit store and the store contract suite

The in-process LimitStore with the D4 check-then-commit order, poison
recovery and the D13 sweep, the seven SMA-677 metric names, and one
contract suite that every limit store must pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(rs): add the gateway [limits] config table

backend, a redacted redis_url, the three limits with their D23 caps,
budget_period and [[limits.org]] overrides, with validation that names
each key and rejects a misspelt one (SMA-677).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(rs): add the gateway rate-limited and budget-exhausted refusals

Two 429 GatewayError cases with the D8 types, Retry-After and the
x-should-retry header that the OpenAI SDKs read (SMA-677).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(rs): make the budget period label panic-free for any instant

key_at and label_at_reset clamp an instant outside chrono's range
instead of panicking. The budget refusal falls back to a static
message when the reset instant is out of range (SMA-677).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(rs): add the gateway limits service and the charge guard

Limits::admit resolves the org, skips the store for an empty policy,

# trust anchor for every request the upstream egress client makes, to any host it reaches — not
# for the whole process. Read once at boot. A bare self-signed leaf
# also works when this bundle holds that leaf's own PEM, though a private CA is tidier once
# more than one host is involved.
# extra_ca_bundle_path = "/etc/paigasus/corp-ca.pem"

# --- Metrics (SMA-446 Unit 2: Prometheus `GET /metrics`) ---

# [metrics]
# enabled = true                # default shown; false skips installing the recorder entirely —
#                                # no /metrics route, no metrics-facade recorder in this process
# addr = "127.0.0.1:9091"       # optional separate internal listener; RECOMMENDED for a public
#                                # gateway so /metrics never shares a port with public traffic.
#                                # unset (default) merges /metrics onto http_addr instead. MUST
#                                # differ from http_addr (rejected by GatewayConfig::validate).

# --- DPoP (SMA-700): proof-of-possession tokens on the protected routes ---
#
# Off by default. With enabled = true, a client may send `Authorization: DPoP <token>` with one
# `DPoP` proof header (RFC 9449). The gateway forwards the proof, the method and the path to IAM,
# which checks it against its authn.dpop.forwarded_base_urls. Turn DPoP on in IAM first.
# A 401 then carries `WWW-Authenticate: DPoP algs="ES256 RS256"`. The API-key leg does not run for
# the DPoP scheme. A client must make a NEW proof for each attempt: a retry that sends the same
# proof again is refused as a replay.
# [dpop]
# enabled = false                       # default shown; env GATEWAY_DPOP__ENABLED

# --- Limits (SMA-677): request rate and token budget on POST /v1/chat/completions ---
#
# Off unless this table exists. An unset key means no limit on that dimension. The value 0 is
# rejected. A misspelt key fails the boot. A table with no limit value set builds no store and
# opens no Redis connection. The gateway logs one info line. Refusals: 429 "rate-limited"
# (Retry-After, retryable) and 429 "budget-exhausted" (type "insufficient_quota",
# x-should-retry: false).
#
# [limits]
# backend = "memory"                     # "memory" (default) | "redis"
#   # memory: one process only. With N replicas the limits are about N times the values below.
#   # A restart sets every budget to zero. Use "redis" for more than one replica.
# # redis_url: set GATEWAY_LIMITS__REDIS_URL, never this file. The URL can carry a password.
# # Required for backend = "redis". Rejected for "memory". Use rediss:// outside a private network.
# # Redis requirements:
# #   - Redis 6.2 or later.
# #   - A URL that always reaches the primary. Do not use a replica or Redis Cluster.
# #   - A dedicated instance for limits, or at least a dedicated logical database.
# #   - maxmemory-policy noeviction, or enough headroom that eviction never runs.
# #     An evicted budget key silently resets the budget of that org.
# #   - appendonly yes, if budgets must survive a Redis restart.
# # Redis must be reachable at boot. A gateway with backend = "redis" does not start while
# # Redis is down. After boot, fail-open applies: when Redis is unavailable, the gateway
# # admits requests with no limit and charges no tokens until Redis recovers. See
# # RUNBOOK-observability.md, "Gateway limits: fail-open and Redis requirements".
# principal_requests_per_minute = 60     # unset: no principal rate limit; max 1000000000
# org_requests_per_minute       = 600    # unset: no org rate limit (summed over the org's principals); max 1000000000
# tokens_per_period             = 5000000 # unset: no token budget; max 1000000000000
# budget_period                 = "monthly" # "daily" | "weekly" (ISO week) | "monthly" (default), UTC
#
# Per-org overrides, by org UUID. TOML only: environment variables cannot set an array of
# tables. With backend = "redis", give EVERY replica the same list, or two replicas apply
# different limits to one shared count. A field you leave out keeps the table default.
# [[limits.org]]
# id                      = "0190a100-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a1"
# org_requests_per_minute = 1200
# tokens_per_period       = 20000000
#
# [[limits.org]]
# id     = "0190a100-0000-7000-8000-0000000000b2"
# exempt = true                          # no org rate and no budget; the principal rate still applies
#
# Environment: GATEWAY_LIMITS__BACKEND, GATEWAY_LIMITS__REDIS_URL,
# GATEWAY_LIMITS__PRINCIPAL_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE, GATEWAY_LIMITS__ORG_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE,
# GATEWAY_LIMITS__TOKENS_PER_PERIOD, GATEWAY_LIMITS__BUDGET_PERIOD.
#
# Charging: a stream is charged its reported usage only when the client sends
# stream_options: {"include_usage": true} (the console playground does). Otherwise the gateway
# charges an estimate: about one token per streamed record plus the prompt text / 4.

# --- Tool-call interception (SMA-749): hold, check and rewrite model tool calls ---
#
# Off by default. With enabled = true the gateway parses every response of
# POST /v1/chat/completions, holds each tool call until its arguments are complete (text keeps
# streaming), asks the decider, and replaces a blocked call with an assistant notice. This build's
# decider allows every call. Each decision is reported as an SSE comment ": paigasus-decision {...}"
# or, for a non-stream answer, in the paigasus-tool-decisions header. A misspelt key fails the boot.
#
# [tool_interception]
# enabled             = false      # env GATEWAY_TOOL_INTERCEPTION__ENABLED
# max_record_bytes    = 1048576    # one SSE record; larger is a failure
# max_held_bytes      = 4194304    # all held bytes of one stream; also the cap on one non-stream body
# max_hold_secs       = 300        # from a tool call's first fragment to its completion
# decide_timeout_secs = 5
# keepalive_secs      = 10         # ": keep-alive" comment while a call is held; < max_hold_secs
# on_failure          = "block"    # "block" (default) | "allow" (observe: forward and report)
#   # A failure is: a record or body that is not strict JSON or not the provider's shape, a
#   # limit above, a decider error, or a stream that ends inside a tool call. With "block", a
#   # non-stream answer that cannot be checked is a 502 "tool-interception-malformed-response".
#
# SMA-769: the OpenAI Responses API route, POST /v1/responses. Off by default; with
# enabled = false the route answers 404. Setting it back to false is the rollback.
#
# [responses]
# enabled           = false      # env GATEWAY_RESPONSES__ENABLED
# max_request_bytes = 16777216   # env GATEWAY_RESPONSES__MAX_REQUEST_BYTES; over this is a 413
# max_record_bytes  = 16777216   # env GATEWAY_RESPONSES__MAX_RECORD_BYTES; one SSE record
# max_held_bytes    = 33554432   # env GATEWAY_RESPONSES__MAX_HELD_BYTES; all held bytes of one stream
#   # Operator notes (spec 9):
#   # 1. The gateway does not rewrite "store". With store = true (the OpenAI default),
#   #    OpenAI keeps the output, a blocked call included, for its retention period.
#   # 2. Hosted execution: OpenAI runs a hosted "shell_call" or a server "tool_search_call"
#   #    itself, even when the report says "block". The gateway cannot hold it, because the
#   #    item class is fixed before these fields are known. The notice replaces the item for
#   #    the client only. The decision log must not count such a block as a prevented action.
#   # 3. With interception on, the route refuses with 400 "responses-stateful-not-supported"
#   #    a request that asks for state on the server. These are: a non-null
#   #    "previous_response_id", "conversation" or "prompt", and an "item_reference" input
#   #    item. An input item with no string "type" and no string "role" counts as an
#   #    "item_reference". "background": true is refused in both modes.
#   # 4. With interception on, the route refuses a request body that has a duplicate JSON key
#   #    at any depth (400, before admission). A duplicate "background" key is refused in
#   #    both modes.
#   # 5. Observe mode ("on_failure" = "allow"): when one item is truncated, the response
#   #    switches to pass-through. A completed call that the policy blocks, in the same
#   #    response, can then reach the client. A stream and a body behave the same.
#   # 6. Rollback: set "enabled" = false. The route then answers 404.
#
# SMA-752: Cedar tool-call decisions (spec 6.4). Off by default; with enabled = false the
# gateway behaves as before. A misspelt key fails at start. Needs [tool_interception] enabled.
#
# WARNING: mode "enforce" with no tenant policies blocks every tool that is not on the floor.
# Cedar denies by default, and no policy permits the call. Load a permit policy for an org
# before you set its mode to "enforce". Use "log_only" first to see what the policy would block.
# A blocked shell_call_output becomes one notice chunk; the real upstream accepts it (SMA-776).
# A blocked computer_call_output has no field for the notice. An enforced block refuses the
# request with a 400 tool-result-unreplaceable. A floor block of "computer" does this in every
# mode. See rs/crates/libs/paigasus-gateway-core/tests/fixtures/request_rewrite/README.md.
#
# [tool_policy]
# enabled               = false      # env GATEWAY_TOOL_POLICY__ENABLED
# on_policy_unavailable = "closed"   # REQUIRED when enabled: "open" | "closed" (D9, D34)
# default_mode          = "off"      # "off" | "log_only" | "enforce"; the mode of an org with no entry (D8)
# refresh_secs          = 30         # 1..=86400
# max_stale_secs        = 300        # 1..=86400; >= refresh_secs
# idle_evict_secs       = 3600       # 1..=86400
# load_timeout_ms       = 1000       # must be < tool_interception.decide_timeout_secs * 1000 (D31)
# source = { kind = "file", dir = "/etc/paigasus/tool-policies" }   # REQUIRED when enabled
#   # SMA-775: source = { kind = "iam" } fetches the compiled sets and the tenant settings (mode and
#   # fail mode) from paigasus-iam. It needs iam.service_credential_file. [[tool_policy.org]]
#   # entries are refused with it, because IAM holds the mode and the fail mode of each org.
#   # The floor is always enforced when enabled (D33). There is no floor_mode.
#
# [tool_policy.nats]                 # optional: policy invalidation events
# url        = "nats://nats:4222"    # never written to logs or dumps
# creds_file = "/etc/nats/creds"
# ca_file    = "/etc/nats/ca.pem"
#
# [[tool_policy.org]]                # TOML only; one entry per org (D7, D34)
# id                    = "0190a100-0000-7000-8000-0000000000a1"
# mode                  = "enforce"
# on_policy_unavailable = "open"     # optional override of the global value

# --- SMA-755: the tool decision log (§ 5.12) ---
# Records each tool-policy decision in a Redis stream, and a relay publishes it to NATS.
# enabled = true needs [tool_policy] enabled = true, redis_url, digest_key, digest_key_id and [decision_log.nats].
# A Redis outage or a NATS outage at boot does not stop the gateway.
#
# [decision_log]
# enabled        = false                         # env GATEWAY_DECISION_LOG__ENABLED
# redis_url      = "redis://redis:6379"          # required when enabled; never written to logs or dumps
# key_prefix     = "paigasus:gateway"            # default shown; must not be empty or padded
# stream_max_len = 100000                        # default shown; at least 1
# queue_capacity = 4096                          # default shown; at least 1
# digest_key     = "change-me-at-least-32-bytes-long-secret"   # required when enabled; at least 32 bytes; never logged
# digest_key_id  = "2026-11"                     # required when enabled; names the key for a rotation
#
# [decision_log.nats]                            # required when enabled
# url        = "nats://nats:4222"                # never written to logs or dumps
# creds_file = "/etc/paigasus/nats/gateway-decision-publisher.creds"
# ca_file    = "/etc/paigasus/nats/ca.pem"       # optional; REPLACES the system trust store (absent: system roots)

+#
+# An entry lives up to 2 x iat_window_secs, so with the defaults one key can make about 8 proofs a

# Tool policies: tenant guide (SMA-775)

This guide is for an organization admin. It explains how to turn on tool policies and how to
write a policy that works. The operator steps are in
[`docs/ops/RUNBOOK-tool-policies.md`](../ops/RUNBOOK-tool-policies.md).

A tool policy set decides which tool calls the AI Gateway allows for your organization. IAM
stores the set and compiles it. The gateway fetches the compiled set and enforces it.

## 1. Modes and fail modes

Each organization has two settings. Write them with
`PUT /v1/organizations/{id}/tool-policy-settings` (gRPC `PutToolPolicySettings`). The body is
`{"mode": "...", "fail_mode": "..."}`. Read them with `GET` on the same route. You need the
`ManageToolPolicySettings` action for the write and the `ReadToolPolicies` action for the read.
The `org_admin` role has both.

| `mode` | What the gateway does with your set |
|---|---|
| `off` | The gateway does not use your set. This is the default. |
| `log_only` | The gateway evaluates your set and records a block, but it does not block the call. |
| `enforce` | The gateway blocks every call that your set does not permit. |

The fail mode applies only in `enforce` mode. It tells the gateway what to do when it cannot load
your set.

| `fail_mode` | What the gateway does in `enforce` mode when it cannot load your set |
|---|---|
| `closed` | The gateway blocks the call. This is the default. |
| `open` | The gateway allows the call and reports it. |
## 4. Held versions

A new compiler or schema version can change how IAM compiles your set. IAM compiles your live
set again after such a change. If the output is the same, your set gets a new live version with no
action from you. If the output is different, or the compile now rejects the set, IAM keeps your
live version and stores a held version.

A held version is a proposal. The gateway never reads it. Your live set keeps working with no
change. IAM publishes no event for a held version.

1. List the held versions of your organization with
   `GET /v1/organizations/{id}/held-tool-policy-versions` (gRPC `ListHeldToolPolicyVersions`). You
   need the `ReadToolPolicies` action.
2. Read the `report` of each row. It shows the policies, conditions and schema names that differ.
   For a rejected set, it shows the rejections.
3. Accept the row with `POST /v1/organizations/{id}/held-tool-policy-versions/{version}/accept`
   (gRPC `AcceptHeldToolPolicyVersion`). Discard it with the same route and `/discard` (gRPC
   `DiscardHeldToolPolicyVersion`). You need the `ManageToolPolicies` action for both.

An accept makes the held output your next live version. Your own save of the set also replaces the
held version, because it makes a new live version. A rejected set has no output and you cannot
accept it. Change the source and save the set instead.

While a held version waits for your decision, your live set stays at the old compiler. After a
discard, IAM does not propose the same result again for the same live version and the same
compiler. In both cases, a write of your tool catalog is refused with
`tool-policy-recompile-pending`. In the first case, you accept the held version to clear this.
If the compile rejected the set, the held version has no output and an accept returns
`tool-policy-held-not-acceptable`. Correct the source and save the set to clear this. In the
second case, there is no held version, so you save the set again. In the first case, you can also
save the set again.

A save of the set or a discard removes the held version. An accept or a discard of that held
version after the save or the discard returns `tool-policy-version-not-found`. List the held
versions again.

An accept of a held version that still exists but is no longer current returns
`tool-policy-version-conflict`. This occurs when the compiler, the schema or the catalog changed
after IAM made the held version, or when a save of the set commits during the accept. List the
held versions again and use the current row, or save the set.

    * feat(contracts): add the rate-limited and budget-exhausted gateway reasons
    
    Two gateway registry reasons for SMA-677, regenerated for Rust, Python
    and TypeScript. The SDK gains the quota-exhausted presentation, and both
    console copy tables gain its row.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): add the gateway rate-window arithmetic
    
    The D3 sliding-window counter of SMA-677 as pure domain functions, with
    the integer form that both limit stores share. src/domain.rs moves to
    src/domain/mod.rs.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): add the gateway budget periods, policy and limit store port
    
    UTC daily, ISO-weekly and monthly budget periods with a relative charge
    TTL, the per-request policy with org overrides and exemptions, the D8
    refusal precedence, and the async LimitStore port with its fail-open
    error kinds (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): add the memory limit store and the store contract suite
    
    The in-process LimitStore with the D4 check-then-commit order, poison
    recovery and the D13 sweep, the seven SMA-677 metric names, and one
    contract suite that every limit store must pass.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): add the gateway [limits] config table
    
    backend, a redacted redis_url, the three limits with their D23 caps,
    budget_period and [[limits.org]] overrides, with validation that names
    each key and rejects a misspelt one (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): add the gateway rate-limited and budget-exhausted refusals
    
    Two 429 GatewayError cases with the D8 types, Retry-After and the
    x-should-retry header that the OpenAI SDKs read (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * fix(rs): make the budget period label panic-free for any instant
    
    key_at and label_at_reset clamp an instant outside chrono's range
    instead of panicking. The budget refusal falls back to a static
    message when the reset instant is out of range (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): add the gateway limits service and the charge guard
    
    Limits::admit resolves the org, skips the store for an empty policy,
    applies the D8 precedence and fails open on a store error. ChargeGuard
    charges an admitted request at most once from Drop and writes the
    chat completion metered line (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): add the gateway SSE usage scanner and token estimates
    
    UsageScanner reads a copy of a forwarded stream with all three SSE line
    endings, a bounded record buffer and the usage-object match. The D14
    request and completion estimates for the charge (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): apply the gateway limits in the chat handler
    
    The handler admits through Limits after the body and streaming checks,
    maps a refusal to its 429 or 500, and gives the charge guard the request
    estimate, the usage of a non-stream answer and the stream (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): charge a gateway stream from its usage record
    
    The stream relay feeds a copy of every chunk to the usage scanner, so a
    stream is charged its reported total, or one token per record, once,
    also on a mid-stream error or a client disconnect (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): add the Redis limit store to the gateway
    
    One Lua admission script that checks every key and then counts, a
    MULTI INCRBY EXPIRE charge with a relative TTL, spawned on a TaskTracker,
    and the D10 error kinds over the paigasus-redis breaker (SMA-677).
    The error detail holds the kind and code only, never the URL.
    The paigasus-redis docs are now service-neutral.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * test(rs): run the gateway limit store against real Redis
    
    The contract suite on redis 6.2 and 7.4 through a new pinned-image
    helper in paigasus-test-docker, the TTL, key, NOSCRIPT and OOM cases, a
    two-replica end-to-end test, a Docker canary, and the nextest retry and
    container-cap overrides for the gateway (SMA-677).
    
    The admission script now raises an error on a stored count that is not
    an integer, before any write, so the all-or-nothing rule holds. The
    shared suite gains the D3 clamp boundary rows.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(rs): boot the gateway limits and drain charges at shutdown
    
    build_limits primes the limit series and builds the memory or the eager
    Redis store after the metrics recorder exists; supervise drains the
    spawned charges for at most 5 s and counts the rest (SMA-677).
    A charge that arrives after the drain closed the tracker is counted as
    shutdown. The boot error for a failed Redis connect names the error kind
    only, never the URL.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(repo): alert on a gateway limits fail-open outage
    
    GatewayLimitsRedisBreakerOpen watches the limits breaker gauge, and
    GatewayLimitStoreUnavailable catches short outages and server or decode
    errors that never open the breaker, with promtool firing and quiet
    cases (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * test(repo): pin the gateway fail-open alert cases
    
    Add a kind=server case with a closed breaker, a breaker recovery case,
    and a half-open case, so a narrower expr no longer passes (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * docs(docs): document the gateway limits and their Redis requirements
    
    The [limits] section of gateway.toml.example, the seven metric families,
    the metered log line, two alert entries, the fail-open and Redis
    requirements section, and the chart replicas note (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * feat(ts): ask for stream usage from the gateway console playground
    
    The playground sends stream_options.include_usage, so the gateway charges
    a playground stream from its reported usage (SMA-677).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * fix(rs): apply the SMA-677 final-review fixes
    
    Rewrite the SMA-677 prose in Simplified Technical English. Document the empty
    [limits] table (D11). Log one info line when a limit store is built. Correct
    the dto comment on message content. Add a blank line before the test module.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    
    * docs(docs): finish the STE pass on the gateway limits runbook
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

iam_extra = """
- A new table, `[tool_policies]`, turns on the tool catalog and the tool policy sets of an
  organization. It is off by default (`enabled = false`). With `enabled = true`, IAM runs the
  policy compiler child process `compiler_path` once at boot. If the compiler is missing, IAM
  still boots and the feature reports `capability-disabled`. The table also sets the compiler
  limits: `compile_timeout_ms`, `max_source_bytes`, `max_result_bytes`, `rlimit_as_bytes`,
  `rlimit_cpu_secs`, `compiler_permits` and `max_window_secs`. It sets the catalog limits:
  `max_tools`, `max_input_schema_bytes`, `max_schema_depth` and `max_catalog_response_bytes`
  (SMA-774).
- IAM gets a tool catalog for each organization, and a tool policy set with a version history.
  The routes are `/v1/organizations/{id}/tools`, `/v1/organizations/{id}/tool-imports`,
  `/v1/organizations/{id}/tool-policy-set` and `/v1/tool-policy-floor`. The gRPC API has the same
  calls. IAM compiles a Dogwood policy source to Cedar in a hardened child process (SMA-774).
- Each organization has two tool policy settings: `mode` (`off`, `log_only` or `enforce`) and
  `fail_mode` (`closed` or `open`). Use `PUT` and `GET` on
  `/v1/organizations/{id}/tool-policy-settings`. The new actions are `ManageToolPolicySettings` and
  `ReadToolPolicies`. The `org_admin` role has both (SMA-775).
- IAM serves the compiled tool policies to the gateway on
  `/v1/organizations/{id}/compiled-tool-policies` and `/v1/compiled-tool-policy-floor`. The gateway
  reads them with a service credential, an API key with the new `tool_policy_reader` role
  (SMA-775).
- IAM compiles the live tool policy sets again after a compiler or schema change. When the output
  differs, or the compile rejects the set, IAM keeps the live version and stores a held version. The
  gateway never reads a held version. An admin lists, accepts or discards a held version on
  `/v1/organizations/{id}/held-tool-policy-versions`. A platform admin uses
  `/v1/held-tool-policy-versions`, `/v1/tool-policy-floor/held-versions/{version}/accept` and
  `/v1/tool-policy-recompile`. A write of the tool catalog fails with `tool-policy-recompile-pending`
  while a held version waits. IAM adds the migration `m0015_tool_policy_held_versions`
  (SMA-781).

### Changed

- The policy compiler uses Dogwood 1.2.0 and `cedar-policy` 4.14.0. `COMPILER_GENERATION` is now 2,
  so IAM compiles the live tool policy sets again after the upgrade. Cedar 4.14 prints
  `context.findings.contains` where it printed `(context.findings).contains`. Dogwood 1.2.0 now
  rejects an impossible policy in its own validation step, before the shape and window checks
  (SMA-800).

  longer has a compiled-in Mozilla root list. On Linux, an empty system store with no

gw_extra = """
- A new table, `[limits]`, sets a rate limit and a token budget for `POST /v1/chat/completions`. It
  is off unless the table exists. The settings are `principal_requests_per_minute`,
  `org_requests_per_minute`, `tokens_per_period` and `budget_period` (`daily`, `weekly` or
  `monthly`). The `[[limits.org]]` entries set a limit or `exempt = true` for one organization.
  `backend` is `memory` (default) or `redis`. With `redis`, set `GATEWAY_LIMITS__REDIS_URL`. If
  Redis is unavailable after boot, the gateway admits requests with no limit and logs it. A
  refusal is 429 `rate-limited` (with `Retry-After`) or 429 `budget-exhausted` (SMA-677).
- A new table, `[tool_interception]`, holds each tool call of a chat completion until its
  arguments are complete. The gateway asks the decider and replaces a blocked call with an
  assistant notice. It is off by default. A decision is an SSE comment `: paigasus-decision` or,
  for a non-stream answer, the header `paigasus-tool-decisions`. With `on_failure = "block"`, a
  non-stream answer that the gateway cannot check is 502 `tool-interception-malformed-response`
  (SMA-749).
- A new route, `POST /v1/responses`, serves the OpenAI Responses API with the same tool call
  interception. It is off by default (`[responses] enabled = false`), and the route answers 404
  then. With interception on, a request for server-side state is 400
  `responses-stateful-not-supported` (SMA-769).
- A new table, `[tool_policy]`, makes Cedar `InvokeTool` decisions. It is off by default and needs
  `[tool_interception]`. The mode of an organization is `off`, `log_only` or `enforce`.
  `on_policy_unavailable` is `open` or `closed`, and it has no default. The platform floor is
  always enforced. The policies come from a directory (`source.kind = "file"`) or from IAM
  (`source.kind = "iam"`). With `iam`, the gateway needs `iam.service_credential_file`, reads the
  mode and the fail mode of each organization from IAM, and refuses `[[tool_policy.org]]` entries.
  An optional `[tool_policy.nats]` table receives policy invalidation events (SMA-752, SMA-775).
- A blocked `computer_call_output` in `enforce` mode refuses the request with 400
  `tool-result-unreplaceable` (SMA-776).
- A new table, `[decision_log]`, records each tool policy decision in a Redis stream. A relay
  publishes the records to the NATS JetStream stream `GATEWAY_DECISIONS`. It is off by default. It
  needs `[tool_policy]`, `redis_url`, `digest_key`, `digest_key_id` and `[decision_log.nats]`. A
  Redis or NATS outage at boot does not stop the gateway. The release also adds a trace export
  command, metrics and alerts for the log (SMA-755).

### Changed

- The HTTP client of the gateway uses `reqwest` 0.13 with the operating-system trust store. The
  image no longer has a compiled-in Mozilla root list. On Linux, an empty system store with no
  `extra_ca_bundle_path` is a client build error (SMA-809).
- The gateway refuses to boot when `tool_policy.nats.ca_file` is set and the URL is plain
  `nats://`. `async-nats` 0.53 makes a root certificate imply TLS (SMA-809).

### Fixed

- The gateway charges the last SSE record of a stream that ends without a blank line. Before this
  fix, the token budget missed that usage (SMA-730).
- A blocked `shell_call_output` now becomes one schema-valid chunk, with the notice in `stderr`
  and exit code 1. The upstream accepts it (SMA-776).
"""
edit("rs/crates/services/paigasus-gateway/CHANGELOG.md", gw_extra, "## [0.2.0] - 2026-10-01", True)

# `repo:helm-render`

The static gate over `charts/paigasus` (SMA-513 PR 2b). It renders the chart with the pinned
`helm` and asserts properties that `helm lint` and the golden files cannot see. It also runs
every script under `charts/paigasus/tests/`, which nothing else runs in CI.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-22-sma-513-pr2b-helm-render-gate-design.md`, which
replaces § 8 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-19-sma-513-multi-zone-ingress-helm-design.md`.

## Modes

| Command | Does |
| -- | -- |
| `bash ci/helm-render/run.sh` | Checks 1–4 and 7 (`helm_render.py --chart charts/paigasus`), then every `charts/paigasus/tests/*.sh` (checks 5 and 6) |
| `bash ci/helm-render/run.sh --self-test` | `helm_render.py --self-test` (in-process rows over inline YAML and proto text), then the wrapper's rc rows |
| `bash ci/helm-render/run.sh --negative-control` | Each fixture under `fixtures/` must make the module exit 3 with its own named row failed |

`moon run repo:helm-render` runs all three, the two controls first, under `set -euo pipefail`.

## Checks

Every render is `helm template paigasus <chart> --kube-version 1.31.0` with the stub values in
`helm_render.py`'s `STUB_VALUES`. The valid subsets are `iam` and `iam+gateway`. Row 7 is the one
exception: it renders against the kind job's own values files, not `STUB_VALUES`.

| Row | Check | It fails when |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `1a` | The slug mirror | `paigasus.serviceSlugs` in `_helpers.tpl` is not EQUAL to the slug set derived from `enum Capability` in `service_info.proto`, or a TypeScript derivation line changed |
| `1.1 <subset>` | Coupling (AC 2) | The Ingress zone ids, the `PAIGASUS_ZONES` keys or the `PAIGASUS_SERVICES` keys are not each EQUAL to the enabled set |
| `1.2 <subset>` | Routing | An Ingress path routes to a Service whose Deployment serves another `PAIGASUS_ZONE` |
| `1.3 <subset>` | Membership | An enabled zone id is not in the proto-derived slug set |
| `2` | No trace of a disabled zone | Any string key or value of the iam-only render, or its raw text, contains `gateway`, the sentinel host or a value set under `zones.gateway` (case-insensitive) |
| `3a`, `3a-prime`, `3b`, `3c` | Independent rollout (AC 5) | `spec.template` of a Deployment differs, stays equal or survives against the table in spec § 5 check 3. Row `3b` renders both sides of the `appVersion` bump with every `image.tag` cleared (SMA-688): the "bump `appVersion` to roll every pod" contract holds only when the tags are empty |
| `4 iam-http <subset>` | Ports agree | The IAM `http` containerPort, `IAM_HTTP_ADDR`, the Service's `http` port and target, and `PAIGASUS_SERVICES.iam` disagree |
| `4 iam-grpc <subset>` | Ports agree | The IAM `grpc` containerPort, `IAM_GRPC_ADDR`, the Service's `grpc` port and target, and `PAIGASUS_IAM_GRPC_URL` disagree |
| `4 console-port <subset>` | Ports agree | A console's containerPort, `PORT` and its Service's resolved target port disagree |
| `4 security-context <subset>` | Security context | A pod lacks `runAsUser: 65532`, `runAsGroup: 65532`, `runAsNonRoot: true`; a container lacks `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false` or sets an identity key to another value; either level carries `readOnlyRootFilesystem` |
| `7 kind-values` | The kind job's values render (SMA-513 PR 3) | `helm template` with `ci/kind/values/a.yaml`, or with `a.yaml` plus `b.yaml`, exits non-zero. A missing values file is rc 2. A render that runs longer than `HELM_TIMEOUT_S` is rc 2, not a failed row (SMA-679) |

The 0.3.0 bump is done for all four images. Nothing is committed, pushed, stashed or reset. Every verify command passed. The one caveat is that `pnpm install` printed a hook-sync failure (below).

## Changed files (14)
- `rs/crates/services/paigasus-iam/Cargo.toml` (0.2.1 to 0.3.0)
- `rs/crates/services/paigasus-gateway/Cargo.toml` (0.2.0 to 0.3.0)
- `rs/Cargo.lock`: only the two `version` lines of `paigasus-iam` and `paigasus-gateway`. I ran `cargo update -p paigasus-iam -p paigasus-gateway --offline`; it locked 0 other packages.
- `ts/apps/iam-console/package.json` and `ts/apps/gateway-console/package.json` (0.2.0 to 0.3.0). `ts/pnpm-lock.yaml` does not record app versions, so it is unchanged.
- The four `CHANGELOG.md` files: iam, gateway, iam-console, gateway-console.
- `charts/paigasus/values.yaml`: four tags changed (lines 25, 36, 92, 114). `Chart.yaml` `appVersion` is untouched.
- Goldens under `charts/paigasus/tests/golden/`: `iam-only.yaml`, `iam-dpop.yaml`, `iam-and-gateway.yaml` and `iam-and-gateway-httproute.yaml`. I edited the image lines with sed. The README names no regeneration tool.
- The gateway backend image (`paigasus-gateway:`) is absent from all goldens, because the chart does not render it. Only its `values.yaml` tag changed.

## Changelogs
All four have a `## [0.3.0] - 2026-11-20` section under an empty `## [Unreleased]`. The date is as you specified. The sources were `git log <last-tag>..HEAD -- <dir>`, commit bodies, `gateway.toml.example`, `iam.toml.example` and the tenant guide. The full section text is in the `CHANGELOG.md` files; this is what each contains.

**iam**
- The existing SMA-700 and SMA-731 entries moved into 0.3.0 unchanged.
- Added entries:
  - The `[tool_policies]` table, with the compiler and catalog limits (SMA-774).
  - The tool catalog, policy sets and routes (SMA-774).
  - The tool policy settings `mode` and `fail_mode` and the new actions (SMA-775).
  - The compiled-policy routes and the `tool_policy_reader` role (SMA-775).
  - Held versions, the recompile route and migration `m0015_tool_policy_held_versions` (SMA-781).
- Changed entries:
  - Dogwood 1.2.0, `cedar-policy` 4.14.0 and `COMPILER_GENERATION` 2 (SMA-800).
  - `reqwest` 0.13 with the OS trust store and no compiled-in Mozilla roots (SMA-809).
  - IAM refuses to boot when `outbox.publisher.root_ca_bundle` is set with a plain `nats://` URL (SMA-809).
- Security entry: the `cedar-policy` move closes GHSA-c33x-vcv4-vg3g (SMA-800).

**gateway**
- The existing SMA-700 entries moved into 0.3.0 unchanged.
- Added entries:
  - The `[limits]` table, with 429 `rate-limited` and `budget-exhausted` (SMA-677).
  - The `[tool_interception]` table (SMA-749).
  - The `POST /v1/responses` route, off by default (SMA-769).
  - The `[tool_policy]` table with `file` and `iam` sources (SMA-752, SMA-775).
  - 400 `tool-result-unreplaceable` (SMA-776).
  - The `[decision_log]` table and the `GATEWAY_DECISIONS` JetStream stream (SMA-755).
- Changed entries: the same `reqwest` 0.13 trust-store change, and a boot refusal when `tool_policy.nats.ca_file` is set with a plain `nats://` URL (SMA-809).
- Fixed entries: the last SSE record charge (SMA-730) and the schema-valid blocked `shell_call_output` (SMA-776).

**iam-console**
- Added:
  - The Paigasus logo in the header and `favicon.ico` (SMA-773).
  - The collapsible sidebar with groups Directory and Administration, the console switcher, and the initials badges (SMA-783).
- Changed:
  - A one-row dialog footer and two contrast fixes (SMA-783).
  - The "Usage limit reached" error copy (SMA-677).

**gateway-console**
- Added and Changed: the same as iam-console, without the groups wording.
- Fixed: the chat playground sends `stream_options.include_usage` (SMA-677).

I skipped test-only, ci-only, docs-only and toolchain commits. These were SMA-806 (Rust 1.100 toolchain), `axum-server` bump #471 and the msw/npm-minor bumps. I also skipped SMA-640 (test-only proxy code) and SMA-755's IAM-side test change. I left out SMA-728, SMA-686 and the older ones because they are already in released sections.

## Grep audit
- Every non-CHANGELOG hit is either a self-test fixture or an older doc, so I changed none:
  - `ci/images/release_decision.py`, `ci/release-plan/release_plan.py`, `ci/images/run.sh` and `ci/helm-render/helm_render.py` hold synthetic version strings.
  - `docs/superpowers/**` is historical.
  - `docs/ops/RUNBOOK-chart.md:14` says "for example `0.2.0`" as an example.
  - `charts/paigasus/README.md:319` says the 0.2.1 IAM image lacks the DPoP proof check. That is still true, so I left it.
- I did not run the exact one-line grep from your brief. I ran a wider one that also includes `*.sh` and `*.py`, and filtered out `docs/superpowers`.

## Verify
- `python3 ci/release-plan/release_plan.py --assert`: rc 0. `ci/release-plan/run.sh` with no argument only prints "one mode is required".
- `bash ci/helm-render/run.sh`: "all checks passed". Rows 8a, 8b and 8c all PASS, and so do `render.sh` (all four goldens) and `refusals.sh`.
- `moon run repo:version-lockstep repo:publish-metadata`: both passed. Lockstep reported "all 20 version-lockstep sites agree". Publish-metadata reported "all checks passed" with no bash-4 error, so no direct re-run was needed. It took 2m38s.
- `cd rs && cargo build -p paigasus-iam -p paigasus-gateway --locked`: it finished (3m36s) and compiled `paigasus-iam v0.3.0` and `paigasus-gateway v0.3.0`.
- `pnpm -C ts install --frozen-lockfile --offline`: "Done". The lockfile is consistent.
- `git diff --stat`: 14 files, 166 insertions and 20 deletions.

## Unsure or worth a look
- The pnpm `prepare` step printed `sync hooks: ❌ could not replace the hook: can't rename commit-msg to commit-msg.old - file already exists`. It changed nothing in the tree. Lefthook hooks may need a manual re-sync.
- The changelog claims come from commit messages, the example configs and the tenant guide. I did not read every code path. The least certain items are:
  - The exact route set and `/v1/tool-policy-recompile` in the iam "held versions" bullet.
  - The iam-console "Usage limit reached" bullet, which is only an error-copy table row.
  - The gateway claim that a Redis outage after boot admits requests with no limit. I took it from the `gateway.toml.example` comments.
- I did not run the full-graph `moon ci`, `repo:actionlint` or `repo:affected-smoke`.
